risks.title: Dependence on strategic suppliers
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the context of sustainable supply chain and engagement with key partners such as Neste, Borealis or Encina. The language is measured but recurring, reflecting growing dependence on specialized suppliers for circular raw materials. The trend is upward due to scaling of recycling projects. This category weighs significantly on industrial operations.

risks.title: Increased competition on sustainable materials
risks.score_rationale: The document emphasizes sustainable solutions as a competitive advantage, but does not explicitly mention competitors. The intensity of language is moderate, but strategic focus on sustainable innovation indicates rising pressure. The trend is upward, and this category is central to product differentiation.

risks.title: Growing regulation on plastics and waste
risks.score_rationale: The risk is strongly implicit in massive investments in chemical recycling (BioBTX, Encina) and ISCC PLUS compliance. The language is proactive but reflects anticipated regulatory pressure. The trend is upward, and European circular economy regulation weighs heavily on the industrial model.

risks.title: Cybersecurity linked to AI and digitalization
risks.score_rationale: Growing use of AI (such as virtual assistant, production line control) is presented as a strategic lever. The language is positive, but increased exposure to cyber threats is implicit. The trend is upward, although the risk is not explicitly mentioned in the filing.

risks.title: Technology dependence on chemical recycling
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights key partnerships (BioBTX, Encina) and investments in recycling technologies not yet proven at scale. The language is enthusiastic but reveals significant exposure. The trend is upward, and strategic success depends on these innovations.

risks.title: Intellectual property protection
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly mentioned, the strong emphasis on innovation (bio-based aniline, AI, recycling processes) implies dependence on patents and know-how. The language is neutral, but the trend is upward with accelerating R&D. The category is critical for differentiation.

risks.title: Availability of renewable raw materials
risks.score_rationale: The transition to renewable raw materials (such as plant sugars for aniline) is central to the strategy. The language is positive but masks supply risks. The trend is upward, and supply chain security is crucial for sustainable production.

ai_positioning.summary: Covestro does not mention any strategy or initiative related to artificial intelligence in its 2024 annual report. The company focuses on materials innovation, recycling and sustainability.
evidence: No mention of AI in strategy, R&D or digitalization sections
Priority given to recycling technologies and bio-based materials
Absence of references to advanced automation or predictive data analytics
